_comment: The permission grant an unattended `/kit:observe file <slug>` session runs under, started by ship-startable.sh --observations once per record. It may read the repository and the store, file one issue, and write its reply, and nothing else — the runner adds the one write rule, scoped to the reply directory it creates for the run, and denies writes to the repository by its path — never a bare Edit deny, which covers Write too and would cancel the reply rule — so the session cannot rewrite the repository or the store: it commits nothing, pushes nothing, edits no file in the repository, and drops no record — the runner drops a record only once the issue it became has a pull request or a park. ship-settings.json denies `gh issue create` for every other session in the run, which is why filing gets a grant of its own rather than a widened one.
